note: Science section, 14-day window (freshness.py 'science' = 336h; window_hours(now_iso) with no section returns the design default 72, so 336 is set explicitly). items.title: Machine learning predicts forest soil fungal diversity from drone images
items.excerpt: University of Alberta researchers combined drone imagery with machine learning to predict below-ground fungal diversity without digging. Integrating remote sensing, soil measurements and ML gives a scalable substitute for labor-intensive manual sampling across vast forests.

items.title: New AI model reveals the volume of the world's glaciers
items.excerpt: Ca' Foscari University of Venice built IceBoost v2.0, a machine-learning model that maps global glacier ice volume from millions of thickness measurements. It puts Earth's glaciers at roughly 150,000 cubic kilometers of ice — 32.3 cm of sea-level rise if fully melted.

items.title: AI method reveals hidden patterns in microbial communities in the Warnow Estuary
items.excerpt: Leibniz Institute for Baltic Sea Research scientists repurposed an AI text-analysis method for ecology, resolving five seasonally successive microbial subcommunities in an estuary. The approach matched or beat conventional statistical analysis of the same data.

items.title: OpenAI's latest math breakthroughs commit research misconduct, experts say
items.excerpt: OpenAI's Astra model announced 10 mathematical advances, but mathematicians say the write-ups reuse existing results from 2016 and 2019 without adequate attribution. The dispute turns AI-for-science from a capability question into a credit-and-provenance question.

items.title: Can AI make mathematics more human?
items.excerpt: Mathematician Yang-Hui He argues AI is changing how mathematical work actually gets done. He says AI 'strangely makes mathematics more human' by forcing specialists in different fields to talk to each other again over shared machine-found ground.

items.title: Is AI Reasoning Right for the Wrong Reasons?
items.excerpt: Reasoning models keep solving hard problems, yet researchers still disagree on whether anything like reasoning is happening inside them. Quanta walks through the experiments pulling apart genuine inference from very good statistical pattern-matching.

items.title: Advancing AMIE towards expert-level audio-visual clinical consultations
items.excerpt: Google Research extended AMIE to real-time video consultations that interpret what the patient shows on camera as well as what they say. In a randomized study with board-certified physicians, AMIE (Video) rated on par with primary care physicians on history-taking and diagnostic accuracy.

items.title: Science One Framework: A verifiable autonomous research framework via Chain-of-Evidence
items.excerpt: Google's Science One prototype attacks the hallucinated-citation problem in AI research agents by forcing every claim onto a traceable evidence chain. It reported zero phantom references while matching expert performance on benchmark research tasks.

items.title: The Telescope That Points Itself
items.excerpt: An AI trained on years of Dark Energy Survey observing decisions now schedules and points the 4-metre Víctor M. Blanco Telescope in real time. Across two 2026 campaigns it matched human expert observers, with headroom to beat them on scarce night-time allocation.

items.title: Seven Needles, 800,000 Haystacks
items.excerpt: An Ohio State team turned a neural network loose on 800,000 quasars and pulled out seven genuine gravitational lenses, roughly doubling the known sample. The lenses are the tool astronomers use to weigh supermassive black holes and their host galaxies.

items.title: AI sniffs out tuberculosis in breath's chemical signature
items.excerpt: Researchers in Botswana and South Africa trained machine learning on the volatile organic compounds in exhaled breath to detect tuberculosis. Support vector machines decoded the chemical signature at 93% accuracy, pointing to a cheap non-invasive screen.

items.title: TutorMoments: Do AI tutors know when to help and when to hold back?
items.excerpt: Ai2 released a framework that measures whether frontier language models know when to withhold help so a student can struggle productively. It reframes tutoring evaluation from answer accuracy to pedagogical timing.

items.title: Nurses seek a seat at the table as they fight expanding clinical AI
items.excerpt: Nurses, the largest slice of the health workforce, are pushing to be involved in how clinical AI gets built and deployed rather than handed the finished tool. Educators and researchers are building channels to bring them into design decisions before deployment.

items.title: AI won't enhance physician autonomy. It will further diminish it
items.excerpt: Former ENT surgeon Frances Mei Hardin argues medical AI is inserting itself into clinical judgment without meaningful physician input. She notes 81% of doctors now use AI professionally, with adoption running well ahead of consent and oversight.
